A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SubCoOp research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material are readable and support comparison despite some internal numerical inconsistencies.

before.justification: V1 reports original SubCoOp experiments, including OOD detection results, component ablations, sensitivity analyses and appendix ID-classification results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds hard-OOD comparisons and evaluations of subspace regularization with OSPCoOp.

M1.justification: The region-selection rule, prompt-defined subspaces, regularization losses, confidence-weighted objective and GL-MCM inference remain unchanged. Remark 1 newly documents inverse stabilization and weight decay without establishing that their implementation changed; OSPCoOp-SR applies the existing regularization.

E1.justification: V2 adds a distinct within-ImageNet hard-OOD evaluation: ImageNet-100 against ImageNet-10 and ImageNet-20, plus both directions between ImageNet-10 and ImageNet-20 (Table 3). This substantially extends test coverage to semantic confusion among ImageNet class groups alongside the retained external OOD benchmarks.

E2.justification: Table 2 expands its CoOp/LoCoOp comparisons to include SCT/SCT-SR and OSPCoOp/OSPCoOp-SR; SCT-SR matches SubCoOp rather than introducing another independent method. Table 1 retains its comparator set. The new hard-OOD table actually compares against SCT, although its caption incorrectly names LoCoOp.

E3.justification: Retained experiments keep the stated shot counts, backbones, SGD settings, 25-epoch budget, scoring functions and evaluation metrics. The new hard-OOD table specifies additional dataset pairings but does not document a distinct split construction or revised training/testing procedure beyond that coverage.

E4.justification: V2 adds hard-OOD robustness comparisons and extends the existing SR-transferability analysis to OSPCoOp. Most component, shot-count, backbone and hyperparameter analyses remain. AUROC curves for the SR-weight and rank-threshold sweeps are removed, reducing the evidence displayed for those retained analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions state that the main results average three random trials and report standard deviations. No new seed information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure appears. Revised means and deviation values change results rather than the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes SubCoOp's reported average FPR95/AUROC from 26.08/93.95 to 25.47/94.07 under the same stated 16-shot benchmark, although v2 Table 9 retains the old values. Table 6 changes ID accuracy from 71.27% to 70.57%; several few-shot, ablation and sensitivity entries also change. New hard-OOD and OSPCoOp results substantially extend the evidence, including OSPCoOp-SR's 24.66 FPR95 and 94.62 AUROC in Table 2.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the complementary projector's identity matrix from I_M to I_D, resolving its dimensional incompatibility with the D-dimensional feature space. Remark 1 also adds a per-feature projection complexity estimate and discussion of rank and inverse conditioning. No theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: V2 adds an explicit negligible-computational-overhead contribution and emphasizes broad integration with existing context-optimization methods. The central claims of improved OOD detection through subspace regularization and preserved ID classification remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds a low-dimensional, class-informative rationale for the shared prompt basis and interprets the new tests as demonstrating hard-OOD robustness. Its across-the-board superiority statement overlooks Table 3's ImageNet-20-to-10 AUROC reversal: 97.72 versus SCT's 97.96. The explicit three-hyperparameter limitation and future subspace-score discussion are removed, while sensitivity discussions remain.

D1.justification: Remark 1 newly describes weight decay and computing the stabilized inverse (W^T W + epsilon I_M)^-1. Numerical values for epsilon and weight decay remain unspecified. The disclosed optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs and GPU are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds positioning against Xu et al.'s OSPCoOp, including its claimed inpainting overhead, and cites Bhalla et al. (2024) and Zhu et al. (2023) to motivate CLIP feature geometry. It removes the earlier selective-subspace-projection reference to Zhu et al. (2024) and changes several supporting citations. The appendix's broad related-work organization remains largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement and method motivation are selectively rewritten; contributions become enumerated, entropy regularization moves into the background, and sections and appendices receive labels. The notation paragraph and closing limitations/future-work passage disappear. Most experimental and supplementary prose is retained.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two-column to single-column layout with extensive figure and table rearrangement. Main empirical plots are reduced to FPR95 panels, example-image comparisons are rearranged horizontally, Table 2 expands, and a new hard-OOD table appears. Many removed AUROC displays retain their numerical counterparts in appendix tables.

improvement.justification: The added hard-OOD and OSPCoOp comparisons broaden the evidence, and the projector correction and implementation discussion improve clarity. However, v1's matching 16-shot results in Tables 1 and 4 become conflicting results in v2 Tables 1 and 9. V2 also overstates the hard-OOD findings and removes its explicit limitation discussion. These evidence gains and reporting-reliability losses leave the net quality change uncertain.
